articles.title: Beristain toma los mandos del Granada sin paños calientes: "Las cuentas son un problema grave"
articles.standfirst: “Es urgente, importante y necesaria la entrada de un nuevo inversor”, ha confesado en su primera comparecencia como presidente del club nazarí
articles.summary: “Es urgente, importante y necesaria la entrada de un nuevo inversor”, ha confesado en su primera comparecencia como presidente del club nazarí
articles.body: El Granada lleva meses de incertidumbre, sumido en un proceso de venta que no termina de concluir, una etapa de transición que llegó a generar un vacío de poder peligroso para la entidad que ahora se intenta subsanar de forma oficial con la llegada al sillón de mando de Ignacio Beristain, una solución intermedia mientras se consuma el traspaso de poderes. El nuevo mandatario del conjunto rojiblanco, que lleva todo el verano trabajando entre bambalinas asumiendo la planificación deportiva, se ha sentado por primera vez ante los medios para hacer una radiografía del club de la forma más transparente y honesta, principios que van a regir esta nueva estaba que se abre en el Granada. Sobre el proceso de venta, Beristain se ha mostrado optimista, aunque no ha podido ofrecer plazos sobre el desenlace final: “El proceso sigue avanzando, todos en la ciudad conocéis la complejidad a la que está sujeto el proceso. Todas las partes hemos llegado a ese principio de acuerdo y la intención es terminar de cerrar la operación con el cambio de propiedad. Todavía no se ha llegado a ese cierre formal pero se está trabajando en ello. Tenemos la fortuna de que hay un comprador que está enamorado del club y está decidido a llevar la operación a buen término”, ha reconocido. Un proceso de venta que se ha convertido en vital para que la entidad pueda solucionar sus problemas económicos, como ha confesado: “Es urgente, importante y necesaria la entrada de un nuevo inversor, no tanto por lo que vayan a pagar por las acciones, es por la aportación que tiene que hacer que está prevista y presupuestada en esa plan de inversión a medio y largo plazo”. Sobre la realidad económica de la entidad granadina Beristain también ha sido muy claro, cifrando el déficit en 20 millones de euros: “Las cuentas y la situación son un problema grave, no hay que esconderlo, requiere soluciones y planes de acción para que poco a poco cambiemos el rumbo como hace cualquier familia que ha gastado más de lo que entraba en casa. Queremos ser sostenibles y la obligación del Consejo será tomar las medidas para poner en buen rumbo al club de manera gradual pero de manera firme”. “Estamos trabajando para intentar equilibrar las cuentas, que es algo fundamental y necesario, como administradores es en lo que nos tenemos que centrar ahora mismo. Eso hace más importante que podamos llevar a buen término la operación de cambio de control por la situación crítica que tiene el club a nivel financiero”, ha añadido. Pero no todo son nubarrones negros en el horizonte del Granada, que ha comenzado el curso de forma inmejorable, con un equipo que se ha encaramado a lo más alto de la tabla: “Nos hemos encontrado un equipo que transmite lo que se ve en el campo, que transmite energía, solidaridad y ambición, es con lo que nos hemos encontrado y lo que hemos intentado construir. Entendemos el potencial que tiene el club gracias a su afición, a la ciudad y a su historia, somos ambiciosos, pero el futuro inmediato pasa por ser competitivos y crecer, no son palabras huecas”. Tampoco ha dudado el nuevo presidente del Granada en deshacerse en elogios con Pacheta: “Tenemos la suerte y la fortuna de tener a un míster espectacular en muchos aspectos y también en su interacción personal. Es un entrenador con el que ya había hablado en el pasado y con el que quise trabajar y la primera vez que hablamos en el Granada él me lo recordó. Tenemos un gran entrenador y somos afortunados de tener a Pacheta con nosotros”. Beristain asume el bastón de mando en el Granada con un mensaje claro para el granadinismo: “Trasladarles mi compromiso para devolver la estabilidad al club y sentar las bases para mirar al futuro con confianza e ilusión”.

articles.title: De la Fuente arropa a Ceuta: "Sois mis ídolos, no estáis solos"
articles.standfirst: El seleccionador aseguró que el pueblo de Ceuta tiene el apoyo de todos y cada uno de los españoles
articles.summary: El seleccionador aseguró que el pueblo de Ceuta tiene el apoyo de todos y cada uno de los españoles
articles.body: "España es Ceuta y Ceuta es España". Fueron las palabras de Rafael Louzán en representación de la delegación de la Real Federación Española de Fútbol que se desplazó a Ceuta para mostrar su apoyo a la ciudad. El presidente, junto al seleccionador, Luis de la Fuente; el secretario general, Álvaro de Miguel; y el director deportivo, Aitor Karanka; se desplazaron este viernes a la ciudad autónoma para compartir con los ceutíes el éxito de nuestro fútbol y, sobre todo, para mandarles un mensaje de ánimo y apoyo en este momento tan complicado. Las circunstancias meteorológicas retrasaron el inicio del acto, pero no disminuyeron la intensidad del mensaje que Louzán y De la Fuente querían hacer llegar en el Palacio de la Asamblea, donde fueron recibidos por Juan Jesús Vivas, presidente de la Ciudad Autónoma, a quien le ofrecieron la Copa Mundial lograda este verano tras fundirse con él en un emotivo abrazo. "Ceuta, sin desearlo, se ha convertido en el epicentro de la actualidad española y europea, pero la visita de la RFEF viene a tocarnos el corazón y el alma. No exagero si digo que el fútbol es un fenómeno de una trascendencia enorme porque desata pasiones, estimula y mueve el ánimo de las personas. El fútbol une y hay pocas cosas que tengan la capacidad que tiene la selección de unir a todos los españoles. Cuando gana la selección, ganamos todos. Este 19 de julio me sentí muy unido a los ceutíes y a los españoles, así que esa felicidad es de agradecer", aseguró Vivas. Pero el mensaje de agradecimiento no se quedó ahí. Y es que el presidente, emocionado, quiso dirigirse directamente a comitiva de la RFEF: "Hoy Rafael Louzán está aquí porque hay que estar con los que sufren y con los que pasan mal. Su visita es aliento para una ciudad que está sufriendo mucho. Pocos días después de ganar el Mundial sufrimos el mayor golpe de la historia de esta ciudad y hoy sois vosotros los que nos ayudáis a mandar el mensaje de que Ceuta no se vende y Ceuta se defiende. Y tú, Luis (De la Fuente) eres la demostración de que puedes llegar a lo más alto sin que se te suba a la cabeza. Lo has tenido más difícil que ningún otro, pero nos has llevado a lo más alto. Eres grande porque eres humilde y porque, para ti, las personas cuentan mucho", sentenció el líder ceutí. Por su parte, Rafael Louzán, quiso dirigirse am pueblo ceutí: "Esta copa del mundo empieza su gira por España y el mejor lugar para iniciar esa gira es Ceuta. Desde la casa del fútbol español queremos seguir dando alegrías. Somos un gran país campeón del mundo masculino y femenino, y eso es gracias al trabajo de las federaciones territoriales como la de Ceuta", explicó el presidente. Por último, Luis de la Fuente cerró el acto asegurando que está "agradecido y emocionado por lo que he vivido en Ceuta". El seleccionador aseguró que "todos los caballas se han convertido en los ídolos del resto de España por la entereza y la responsabilidad con la que estáis asumiendo esta situación. No estáis solos, tenéis a vuestros compatriotas con vosotros y no os vamos a fallar". El mensaje es claro. El fútbol ceutí tiene en apoyo de la Federación para que la temporada se inicie con garantías y con la mayor normalidad posible. Es el gran objetivo y por eso han querido estar en el terreno, para que ese mensaje llegue a todos los clubes de la ciudad. Junto al presidente de la Federación de Fútbol de Ceuta, Antonio García Gaona, los miembros de la RFEF mantuvieron un encuentro junto a un centenar de representantes de futbolistas, árbitros, entrenadores y directivos del fútbol ceutí.

articles.title: Way-Too-Early Predictions for the 2026 Winter Transfer Window
articles.summary: The 2026 summer transfer window for Europe's top leagues has barely concluded, but we're already hungry for more buying and selling.
articles.body:
The 2026 summer transfer window for Europe's top leagues has barely concluded, but we're already hungry for more buying and selling.

Of course, a single window can't solve all of a club's problems at once, or forever, so there's always room to improve and opportunities to exploit.

Ahead, we've identified a few likely moves a handful of top clubs will make when the winter buying period opens up.

In the dying embers of the summer window, Manchester United made an inquiry for Manchester City left-back Rayan Ait-Nouri, according to ESPN .

The late move was an unusual strategy, since it's a serious position of need for the Red Devils. Luke Shaw is the current starter, but the 31-year-old is far below the standard required for a club challenging for a Premier League title and in Europe.

Instead, United used the signing period to focus on a midfield rebuild rather than addressing issues in the backline. Youri Tielemans, Andrey Santos and Carlos Baleba arrived to revamp the engine room, leaving other areas of the squad completely unaddressed.

Ideally, a right-back, a center-back and potentially another striker should be on the shopping list for winter, but the left-back position is the most glaring area in need of an upgrade.

The club could return for Ait-Nouri, but Lewis Hall should be considered a top priority. The Newcastle United player has proved to be dependable in his defensive duties while also offering plenty in the final third.

The soon-to-be 22-year-old could represent the Red Devils at a high level for the best part of the next decade, but he will not come cheap.

Compared to their other Big Six counterparts, Liverpool had a fairly quiet window, putting their focus mainly into the pursuit of Paris Saint-Germain's Bradley Barcola, which eventually proved successful.

However, there are other positions in need of reinforcement, not least at right back.

In a pre-season press conference, Andoni Iraola put his faith in Conor Bradley, who is in recovery from a long-term injury.

"I think it is a situation that is tricky, because we trust Conor in the long term, we know, we want him to be our right back, but right now he is still a little bit far from returning," the Spaniard told reporters.

However, this isn't the Northern Irishman's first stint in the injury room, and his fitness issues could quickly come back to haunt the Reds.

Elsewhere in the position, Jeremie Frimpong has so far not demonstrated the quality he showed at Bayer Leverkusen, and former coach Arne Slot even favored him in a more advanced role. Meanwhile, Joe Gomez is another regular injury worry, and putting Ronald Araujo there would further deplete an already thin center-back corps. Using Dominik Szoboszlai has proved effective, but it deprives the Reds of their best midfielder.

Liverpool should also look into a battling No. 6, who can provide a little extra support to a creaky back line and allow the forward players, not least Florian Wirtz, to focus their efforts on the final third.

But the situation on the right could become more pronounced quickly, especially if injuries continue to be a problem.

Among the most dramatic transfer sagas of the window was Julián Alvarez's attempt to engineer an exit from Atlético Madrid to Barcelona.

The Argentinian made his intentions to move to the Camp Nou very clear, but Atleti released a statement saying that "zero consideration" was being given to let the 26-year-old leave the Spanish capital.

The forward missed training sessions to further try to force the club's hand, even rebuffing supposed interest from Arsenal because he had eyes for only one club. But it all came to naught in the end, and he now has the awkward task of winning over his teammates, his coaches, and the Atleti fans.

It's a relationship that seems difficult to repair, and Alvarez will likely try additional tactics to try to get the move of his dreams in the coming months. Barcelona will be watching it all unfold with interest.

The Blaugrana's financial problems seem to be behind them after a summer of spending, making another approach in the winter likely. They have started the season brightly, though, with new winger Anthony Gordon fitting in comfortably alongside Lamine Yamal and Raphinha in the forward line.

But if a player like Alvarez is available, then every effort should be made to make the move happen. Barcelona will not be deterred by the difficulties they faced in the summer and will surely make another attempt.

FIFA Accuses UEFA of 'Smear Campaign' in Court Filing (AP)

Despite the pretty clear warning signs throughout the window, Chelsea failed to do any succession planning for the likely exit of Enzo Fernandez, with his move to Manchester City finally being completed on deadline day.

The club reportedly made late approaches for Roma's Manu Kone and Monaco's Lamine Camara, but both proved unsuccessful.

Both are fine players, but at present, they feel a step below the caliber of player they lost with the Argentinian's departure. With that in mind, the Blues will be looking to make a big splash in the winter window to effectively replace the World Cup-winning midfielder.

The West Londoners received £125 million ($169 million) for Fernandez, a joint-British-record fee, and that money will be burning a hole in the pockets of a club that has made no secret of its love of spending.

A huge bid should be expected for a new midfield general, perhaps in addition to return attempts to sign Camara and Kone. Crystal Palace's Adam Wharton, Liverpool's Alexis Mac Allister, and Bournemouth's Alex Scott could be among the domestic targets.

Viktor Gyökeres scored 14 Premier League goals as Arsenal clinched the Premier League title last term.

That would suggest the Swede was a major part of the Gunners' drought-ending trophy lift, but he only featured in the starting XI in 26 of a possible 36 games, and he didn't feel like a perfect fit in Mikel Arteta's setup.

Gyökeres has been an unused substitute in Arsenal's first two games of the season. While there's a long campaign ahead across multiple competitions, it feels like he is already surplus to requirements at the Emirates Stadium, despite making a reported $74 million move from Sporting CP just last year.

The 28-year-old was tipped as a potential makeweight in a move for Julian Alvarez, and while it doesn't look like the Argentinian will be rocking up in London any time soon, Gyökeres could still be on that radar as a replacement in Madrid.

Either way, clubs will be sniffing around for a player who still has a lot to offer, even if it didn't quite work out in the English capital.

articles.body: El Athletic vuelve a San Mamés después de dos partidos consecutivos como visitantes...y de varios días de revuelo a causa del descontento en distintas estructuras del club que ha generado la decisión de la Junta Directiva de retirar las invitaciones. La medida también la pagará el Atlético, que recibirá el mínimo exigido por reglamento. Y el cupo en cuestión no supera las 30 localidades. En las gradas se hablará de entradas y pases de favor; de la amplia lista de espera para socios con la que el presidente Jon Uriarte ha justificado la retirada de invitaciones para la Asociación de Veteranos del Athletic; de las quejas de un numeroso grupo de empleados por retirarles las suyas y ofrecerles a cambio un seguro médico; de la postura de los expresidentes, también afectados por la quita pero a los que el club ha propuesto tener un asiento vitalicio en el palco -cuando desde la temporada pasada esta directiva decidió vender entradas de palco y experiencias premium por varios cientos de euros-; y también del paso adelante de los jugadores, que han protestado por cuestiones del día a día en el club y Lezama “que ya se van haciendo bola durante cuatro años”. Casi nada. La Catedral no se ha pronunciado todavía al respecto porque no ha tenido oportunidad ya que la tormenta se desató al concluir el partido ante el Barcelona. Desde entonces los únicos que han hablado, y con el freno de mano echado, han sido los jugadores. La dirigencia del club guarda silencio y retrasa el encuentro con los jugadores, los futbolistas dieron su opinión en Barcelona y a Terzic le toca afrontarlo en sus ruedas de prensa. No es muy amigo de estirar el hilo, pero da la sensación de que le encantaría que se diese ya la conversación pendiente. “ Soy consciente de la situación y entiendo el interés, pero es una situación interna del club. Lo mejor es tener una conversación para tratarlo. En el vestuario, lo que está en mis manos es estar preparado al máximo para el partido”, dijo.

articles.title: Marcus Rashford permanently tattoos his Manchester United No. 9 on his body in comeback statement
articles.summary: Football News: Marcus Rashford commemorates his Manchester United comeback with a new tattoo featuring his No. 9 shirt number. This tattoo marks a new chapter for the forward after a challenging period, and highlights his commitment to the team.
articles.body: Marcus Rashford has found a rather permanent way to mark his latest Manchester United comeback.The 28-year-old has added his new No.9 shirt number to a collection of tattoos recording every number he has worn during his senior career. It comes after a turbulent couple of years in which Rashford spent time on loan at Aston Villa and Barcelona, before returning to United this summer and unexpectedly finding himself back in Michael Carrick's plans.Now, with a new number on his shirt and another chapter beginning at his boyhood club, Rashford has put the change in ink too.Rashford's shirt numbers are becoming quite the collectionRashford's abdominal tattoo already featured the No.39, which he wore when he made his Manchester United debut more than 10 years ago, along with the Nos 19 and 10, both of which he has previously worn for the club.He added the No. 14 alongside the No. 9, having worn the former at Barcelona last season and the latter during his six-month spell at Aston Villa. With United handing him the No. 9 again this summer, Rashford has effectively killed two birds with one stone.The numbers sit below a quote reading: "What your eyes see can be misleading, never judge a book by its cover."Rashford showed off the fresh artwork alongside a picture of his new United shirt, captioning the post: "New number, Same mission…"The work was carried out by Manchester tattoo artist Dale McGovern, who has also worked with other footballers including Rashford's United team-mate Ayden Heaven and Leeds defender Jayden Bogle. Rashford even signed a Three Lions shirt for McGovern to display in his studio.There was another addition, too. Rashford had a new tattoo placed below his right ear featuring a flower petal, a feather and the words "Love n let be".The No.9 itself carries a little extra significance because it is one of the most recognisable shirt numbers in United history, having previously been worn by club legends including Andy Cole, Mark Hughes, Bryan Robson, George Best and Denis Law.A new tattoo for a very different Rashford chapterThe timing of the tattoo is particularly interesting given how uncertain Rashford's future at United looked only a few months ago.After spending time on loan at Aston Villa and Barcelona, Barcelona decided against making his move permanent this summer, leaving him back in Manchester with questions over whether he could be reintegrated into the squad.He then came off the bench in United's opening-day defeat by Hull City before starting the 5-2 win over Ipswich Town, his first United start in 626 days.Rashford is also closing in on another personal landmark, sitting on 89 Premier League goals and approaching 100.His performance against Ipswich earned praise from Harry Maguire, who believes the forward can still become a major asset for United if he remains fit, happy and motivated."It's been really good since he came in," Maguire said after the win."He's trained really well and us as players, if Marcus wants to be here and wants to work and wants to improve and wants to help the team, of course, we're willing to have him in the squad."Maguire added: "He's a great talent. You've seen that he's always a threat. I think today, I think he was a threat constantly, and I think he could still do a lot more and I think he'll say that he can do more.""I think if we keep him fit, we keep him happy, he keeps driven, keeps hungry, and I think he is a great asset to have."For now, Rashford's latest career number is safely recorded — although if his United comeback goes particularly well, his tattoo artist may want to keep some space free.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.standfirst: El centrocampista pasará por el quirófano
articles.summary: El centrocampista pasará por el quirófano
articles.body: Los peores presagios se han confirmado. Mikel Rodríguez sufre una rotura del ligamento cruzado anterior de la rodilla derecha y tendrá que pasar por quirófano, por lo que prácticamente dice adiós, a las primeras de cambio, a la temporada de su estreno en el Alavés. La lesión del jugador de Getaria se produjo en el entrenamiento de este jueves en Ibaia, donde notó un crujido en su rodilla que hizo saltar todas las alarmas. Todos los síntomas hacían sospechar que el futbolista sufría una lesión de gravedad, aunque el Alavés optó por mantener la cautela y un mínimo atisbo de confianza. Sin embargo, este viernes ha llegado el jarro de agua fría en forma de parte médico. A sus 24 años, el centrocampista guipuzcoano afronta un largo camino por delante en el que su misión será recuperarse lo mejor posible, sin marcarse fechas de regreso, y con el convencimiento de que volverá a rendir al nivel que ha mostrado hasta ahora. En Mendizorroza había muchas esperanzas depositadas en el futbolista que desembarcó hace escasos dos meses procedente de la Real Sociedad. Una apuesta de presente y futuro, que la Dirección Deportiva llevaba siguiendo mucho tiempo y que en sus primeros tres partidos en Primera ya había dado muestras de su potencial. Una pérdida importante en lo deportivo y también en lo anímico, aunque tiene toda una carrera por delante y al final del túnel en el que acaba de entrar le esperan los mejores años de su carrera.

articles.title: Women's Super League: Birmingham relish challenge of facing WSL champions Man City
articles.summary: Birmingham City head coach Amy Merricks says her side will go "toe-to-toe" with Women's Super League champions Manchester City on their return to the top flight.
articles.body:
Birmingham City head coach Amy Merricks says her side will go "toe-to-toe" with Women's Super League champions Manchester City on their return to the top flight.

Birmingham clinched the WSL 2 title on the final day of last season to secure promotion and end a four-year stint in the second tier, but have been given a tough assignment on the opening day of the 2026-27 campaign.

Merricks' side will travel to the Joie Stadium in Manchester on Sunday (14:30 BST), where a 6-0 defeat in the same fixture in May 2022 condemned them to relegation.

Man City won all 11 of their home WSL matches last season , but Merricks is relishing the challenge awaiting her team.

"I think it's a great time to play Man City. We know it's going to be a challenge but we are well and truly up for it. We are here to compete, not just make up the numbers," Merricks said in her pre-match media conference.

"Our focus is on ourselves, we appreciate and respect who they are and what they have, but our mindset doesn't change."

Last season Birmingham scored an average of 2.09 per game and earned a reputation as an attacking team, something Merricks is not willing to sacrifice just because they will face tougher opposition this term.

"There is a core part of our identity that is non-negotiable for us as Blues and myself as a head coach," she added.

"We are a progressive team, we will find ways to create and score. We are really clear on what our strengths are and what we need to maximise.

"This is the best league in the world, it is going to be tough and a challenge, but what we can't do is lose our strengths. We have to amplify those and put ourselves in the best position possible.

"We have to focus on what we can control and that's how we can compete. We don't fear anyone. I think we showed that in the cup competitions last year."

Man City boss Andree Jeglertz knows that only too well - Sunday's match comes five months to the day since his side were made to work for a 1-0 victory away at Birmingham in the quarter-finals of the Women's FA Cup.

"We had a tough game against them last year. They were tactically very good and destroyed all the space on the field, defending low and their transitioning was very good. There are threats in their team we need to give attention to," Jeglertz said.

"Playing against a team that is new in the league is always a challenge because I know they are coming in with a lot of energy in the first game."

Man City are beginning their first league title defence in a decade, but Jeglertz does not want his side's mentality to change just because they have something to lose.

"We are still chasing, chasing to win again. If you start protecting things, I don't think that will help us. We need to be in a mood of hunger, trying to win again, to compete in different tournaments.

"If we drop a little bit in performance or attitude, teams will go past us."

Jeglertz confirmed that Man City will be without forward Vivianne Miedema until at least late autumn because of a knee injury, while defender Rebecca Knaak will miss the visit of Birmingham with a foot issue.

Defender Jade Rose and midfielder Grace Clinton have returned to training, but summer signing Niamh Charles is "a big question mark" for Sunday.

articles.title: Tottenham Hotspur: Why does Premier League club not have a stadium sponsor?
articles.summary: BBC Sport's Ask Me Anything team explains why after more than seven years, Tottenham Hotspur are yet to agree a stadium sponsorship deal.
articles.body:
Since its opening in 2019, Tottenham Hotspur Stadium has been named as such, with no inclusion of a brand in its title as part of a sponsorship deal.

In this season's Premier League, eight of the 20 clubs have a ground that currently has a sponsorship name. These include Arsenal 's Emirates Stadium, and Manchester City 's Etihad Stadium.

When Tottenham 's ground first opened in the closing months of the 2018-19 season, it was widely believed that shortly after it would be renamed once a sponsorship deal had been agreed.

But after more than seven years of calling the north London ground their home, and operating one of the country's biggest arenas in which to host concerts and NFL matches, the original brand-free name has remained.

No significant progress has been made on a stadium sponsor at present, but the club remain open to acquiring one for their long-term future.

A Tottenham club spokesperson told BBC Sport: "Increasing our revenues through commercial partnerships is crucial for us to be able to remain competitive while staying in the boundaries of financial rules."

The club say that gaining a sponsor is a "key part of the wider suite of opportunities available to potential partners" and that the stadium having the rights to host up to 30 major non-football events per year "increases the value of a naming rights partnership".

"However, we are in a highly competitive industry alongside a number of clubs with similar ambitions, and we will only look to partner with the most-respected, renowned brands that align to our club values and can bring something to our fan experience," they added.

"In addition, we have launched 'The Collective' - a new sponsorship programme designed to deliver bespoke activations to every stand at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium - with Sports Illustrated becoming the first of those partners. ''

articles.title: Why do Tottenham Hotspur not have a stadium sponsor?
articles.summary: BBC Sport's Ask Me Anything team explains why after more than seven years, Tottenham Hotspur are yet to agree a stadium sponsorship deal.
articles.body:
Since its opening in 2019, Tottenham Hotspur Stadium has been named as such, with no inclusion of a brand in its title as part of a sponsorship deal.

In this season's Premier League, eight of the 20 clubs have a ground that currently has a sponsorship name. These include Arsenal's Emirates Stadium, and Manchester City's Etihad Stadium.

When Tottenham's ground first opened in the closing months of the 2018-19 season, it was widely believed that shortly after it would be renamed once a sponsorship deal had been agreed.

But after more than seven years of calling the north London ground their home, and operating one of the country's biggest arenas in which to host concerts and NFL matches, the original brand-free name has remained.

No significant progress has been made on a stadium sponsor at present, but the club remain open to acquiring one for their long-term future.

A Tottenham club spokesperson told BBC Sport: "Increasing our revenues through commercial partnerships is crucial for us to be able to remain competitive while staying in the boundaries of financial rules."

The club say that gaining a sponsor is a "key part of the wider suite of opportunities available to potential partners" and that the stadium having the rights to host up to 30 major non-football events per year "increases the value of a naming rights partnership".

"However, we are in a highly competitive industry alongside a number of clubs with similar ambitions, and we will only look to partner with the most-respected, renowned brands that align to our club values and can bring something to our fan experience," they added.

"In addition, we have launched 'The Collective' - a new sponsorship programme designed to deliver bespoke activations to every stand at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium - with Sports Illustrated becoming the first of those partners. ''

articles.title: Bayern and Schalke at odds over potential Bundesliga playoffs

articles.body:
Ahead of their Bundesliga clash on Saturday, Bayern Munich and newly promoted Schalke are at odds over a potential introduction of championship playoffs in the top tier.

While Schalke's supervisory board chairman, Axel Hefer, spoke in favour of the idea ahead, Bayern president Herbert Hainer rejected the plan in a joint interview conducted by the Bild newspaper on Friday.

"I believe that Bayern, too, should have a strong interest in thinking about the format of the league," Hefer.

"So that they can play in the Champions League every year, but at the same time, there's a little more excitement in the domestic league."

The Munich team has won the league title every season since 2013, interrupted only by Bayer Leverkusen's triumph in 2024.

Schalke, meanwhile, have been waiting for the title since 1958 - before the creation of the Bundesliga and when there was still championship playoffs.

"If I were in your situation, I wouldn't think it's worth striving for the title every year, excitement comes from achieving something that isn't yet certain," Hefer argued.

Hainer replied that, when it comes to the playoffs, they have "fundamentally different views."

"That's where we disagree: I want to win the championship every year!" he said.

The Bayern president isn't a fan of knock-out matches following a league phase.

"Whoever is in first place after 34 matchdays should be crowned German champion," he stressed.

As an argument against playoffs, he mentioned Bayern's basketball team's performance last season: "We were in first place by a wide margin after the regular season, but then lost the final play-off game against Alba Berlin because our team was simply exhausted after 83 games."

The current Bundesliga format already includes a relegation/promotion playoff. The 16th-placed in the top tier face the third-placed in the second division. Critics view this format as unfair and argue that the second division side should be directly promoted.

There's currently no concrete discussions over the introduction of a championship playoff.

articles.body:
Liverpool have dealt a serious blow to one of their own players. There's no real option here: he'll have to leave the club if he wants regular football.

Liverpool confirmed their UEFA Champions League squad this week ahead of their competition kick-off against Atlético Madrid. The Reds sprung a couple of surprises in there, too.

Notably, neither Federico Chiesa nor Wataru Endo were included. They cannot play in the competition going forward and it's a hell of statement from the club.

It's no giant shock with Chiesa. Liverpool have now got a number of wingers, all of whom are ahead of him in the pecking order, and the Italian is currently injured. Perhaps it would have been more of a surprise if he were included in the group.

For Endo, though, it's a massive blow. Liverpool simply don't have another defensive midfielder in the squad and yet they've still decided to exclude him from the group - a sign that they have no intentions of using him.

But why? Liverpool have demonstrated over their opening two fixtures that having someone who can plug the middle of the pitch would be a massive benefit, even if it's just to hold onto a bit of control late on.

Endo, though, isn't wanted for the role. Even when there's a need and he the only specialist , Liverpool would rather use square pegs. And that's about as big a confirmation as you can get that there's no real future at the club.

The Reds will almost certainly call on Endo for the EFL Cup and, if he's still around, the opening rounds of the FA Cup. It's difficult to imagine him getting Premier League minutes, though, and the Champions League is now ruled out.
